output.headline: Police arrest far-right activist Daniel Thomas over Channel dinghy slashing
output.standfirst: Police have arrested the 37-year-old on suspicion of crimes including criminal damage with intent to endanger life
output.bodyHtml:
Police have arrested Daniel Thomas, the far-right agitator and anti-migrant activist, on suspicion of criminal damage with intent to endanger life, two days after he filmed himself slashing the side of a dinghy in the middle of the Channel while a rescuer was on board.

Hampshire and Isle of Wight constabulary said in a statement that a 37-year-old man, of no fixed abode, had been arrested on Wednesday night “on suspicion of destroying ships or fixed platforms or endangering their safety under section 11 of the Aviation and Maritime Security Act 1990”.

Officers said Thomas was also suspected of committing “criminal damage, criminal damage with intent to endanger life, and conduct endangering ships, structures or individuals under section 58 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995”.

Thomas appears to have filmed his own arrest on Wednesday night, and a video was uploaded to his YouTube channel showing the moment, apparently at a garage. An officer told him he had been “involved in criminal damage that has recklessly endangered someone’s life”.

Thomas, who prefers to go by the name Danny Tommo, said: “I understand. I knew this was coming.”

Over the summer Thomas brought together dozens of nationalist protest groups under the umbrella movement Patriot Platform.

He was behind anti-immigration marches by masked men this month in Dover and Portsmouth.
